requirements: Scope: discover the title of PHerc. Paris 4 using any of its scans, including the 2.4 um volumes; specify which scan the image comes from.
Mesh: tifxyz mesh of the surface region containing the title, already including a low-distortion isometric 2D parametrization (flattening).
Image of the virtually unwrapped region showing the title visibly and legibly; the submitter need not read it, papyrologists must be able to.
Illustrate the ink predictions in the spatial context of the title search (as in the organizers 30k-first-title-prize post).
Images generated programmatically from the reconstructed CT volume and the submitted mesh; no manual annotation of characters or text.
Ink model outputs of this region should not overlap with any training data used; do not include overlap between training and prediction regions.
Scale bar of 1 cm on the image, plus pixel and millimetre dimensions of a few representative letters.
Name the image after the tifxyz mesh in the same package.
Reproducible methodology: Docker image for automated software, or instructions plus video for human-in-the-loop work.

False-positive mitigation: demonstrate letters are not hallucinated, e.g. validate on a held-out region with known ground truth (k-fold if trained on it); organizers may run the method on held-out data.
Judged by review teams for technical validity and papyrological plausibility and legibility; discovery must not be made public before the official announcement.

Terms: award at sole discretion of Scroll Prize, Inc.; method open-sourced under a permissive licence to accept; payment info within 30 days; datasets used to train ML models and pseudo-label stages/checkpoints published under CC BY-NC 4.0.

derived_radial_placement.status: derived from official bbox metadata; not an organizer statement
derived_radial_placement.text: The labelled / Grand Prize-era segments (the known text, which the organizers place at the end of the work) have mean bbox half-extents of 9.3-15.4 mm. The spiral strips have 13.9 mm (w010-027, 20260701) and 16.3 mm (w028-037), rising to 32.0 mm (w128-129). So the known end-of-work text lies in the inner third of the 130 windings, about w010-w045 and possibly further inside. The data browser caption 'windings 28-37' agrees. On the organizers' general rule (the title follows the end of the primary text), the expected title region is therefore more likely inward of the last known-text column, toward the core. This agrees with the PHerc. 172 and Scroll 5 precedents. The outermost windings (w122-129) that recon ranked would then be the start of the roll, not the end. This needs a per-vertex winding check (tifxyz x/y/z, not read here) before DECL-P4-2 relies on it.
derived_radial_placement.inner_coverage: No official spiral strip exists for windings w000-w009 in either set (both start at w010-027; live segment listing at 2026-09-26T00:11:02Z has 81 segments and no w00x name). The 1.129 um volume 20260608103018 covers the central region including the umbilicus. The 137 keV ROI 20260323153942 sits near the axis. 1.129 um meshes and 1 um predictions (model 20260709123958) exist for the 20260623 inner strips w010-027 (415.32 cm2) and w028-037 (438.29 cm2), and for 7 of the 11 GP-era segments. The 20260701 inner strips are w010-027 (641.42 cm2) and w028-037 (676.2 cm2), on 2.4 um only.

official_meshes_and_flattening.fact: All 81 segments have mesh/intermediate/ with <id>_original.obj, _normalized.obj and _flattened.obj (e.g. w010-027 flattened.obj 496,990,633 B; 20231210121321 flattened.obj 165,558,241 B), plus tifxyz_original/ and tifxyz_normalized/. The spiral tutorial says render_ink.py concatenates each winding chunk, SLIM-flattens it (flatboi) and renders it with vc_render_tifxyz. So the published -on-<volume>.tifxyz meshes are official meshes that already carry a flattening. Whether that flattening meets the prize's 'low-distortion isometric' standard is not stated, and distortion was not measured. OBJ files were not downloaded (outside the allowed metadata list).

ink_9um_applicability.statement: The model card says the models expect ~9 um isotropic surface volumes. For 2.4 um surface volumes, first pool them to the ~9.6 um isotropic representation (XY pyramid level 2, 4x z mean-pooling) with scripts/prepare_9um_isotropic_input.py. Native ~9 um renders work directly. The models are sensitive to the z-layer offset (--layer-start/--layer-end; averaging nearby z windows helps). Label smoothing puts confident no-ink near 0.25; for display use (p-0.25)/0.5 and keep raw TIFFs for quantitative work.
ink_9um_applicability.applies_to: 20260411134726 (2.4 um) segment surface volumes: yes, the documented path, and the one the Paris 4 labels are aligned to. 1.129 um volume 20260608103018: no documented recipe (it would need a non-integer ~8.5x resampling; not official). 45.532 um: no. The 7.91 um DLS volumes are 'native ~9 um'-like but sit outside the bucket, under the EduceLab licence.
ink_9um_applicability.training_overlap_implication: ink_9um trained on all 8 labelled Paris 4 segments with no held-out Paris 4 case. The prize requires that ink outputs of the title region do not overlap any training data. So a DECL-P4-2 region must exclude the labelled/supervised areas of those 8 segments, and a false-positive check on Paris 4 held-out ground truth is not possible with ink_9um as is (k-fold retraining would be needed).
